response.title: what should i buy to power the essentials for a week after an earthquake
response.answer:
For a 7-day power outage after a major earthquake, I recommend a portable LiFePO₄ battery power station, supplemented by solar panels, rather than relying on a gasoline generator.

The key is to size the system for essentials, not your entire house. You can realistically keep your refrigerator, phones, internet, lights, and some small electronics running for a week with the right setup.

1. How much power do you actually need?

Here is a realistic daily electricity budget for a household of 2–4 people.

Essential

	

Estimated daily consumption




Energy-efficient refrigerator

	

1,200 Wh




Wi-Fi router + modem

	

300 Wh




4 phones

	

80 Wh




LED lighting

	

150 Wh




Laptop

	

150 Wh




Fans / small electronics

	

200 Wh




Total per day

	

2,080 Wh




Total for 7 days

	

14,560 Wh

These are planning estimates. Actual consumption varies considerably by appliance, temperature, and usage.

That means you should plan for roughly 15–18 kWh of usable energy over a week, allowing for some conversion losses.

A 2 kWh power station alone would last roughly one day at this usage level. To make it through seven days, you need either substantially more battery capacity or a reliable way to recharge.

2. What I would buy

EcoFlow DELTA PRO 3 Powerstation 4096 Wh

My preferred option
$3,425.92

4,096 Wh battery, 4,000 W output. Good for a refrigerator and multiple essentials, with expandable storage.

Seller: Hard to Find Camera Store

Anker SOLIX F3800 Portable Power Station - 3840Wh | 6000W

$4,898.00

3,840 Wh battery, 6,000 W output. Especially interesting if you eventually want professionally installed home-circuit backup.

Seller: Anker-US

Jackery HomePower 2000 Plus v2

Lower-cost starting point
$1,299.00

2,048 Wh battery, 2,400 W output. Suitable for a smaller essentials setup, but requires more frequent recharging.

Seller: Jackery

220/400W Lightweight Portable Solar Panel Suitcase

$320.99

Portable solar charging option. Check voltage, connectors, and compatibility with your power station before buying.

Seller: Renogy US

3. How much solar would you need?

For the approximately 2.1 kWh/day load above, here's an illustrative comparison assuming 3 equivalent peak-sun hours per day and 75% net solar charging efficiency.

7-day solar and battery calculator

Solar panel capacity

800 W

Battery capacity

4.1 kWh

Estimated solar energy/day

1.80 kWh

Daily energy deficit

0.28 kWh

Estimated energy is sufficient over 7 days.

Assumes a fully charged battery initially, 85% usable battery energy, and consistent sunshine. Weather, shading, panel orientation and overnight loads can change the result substantially.

For an earthquake, I would favor 800–1,200 W of compatible portable solar panels if you have an unobstructed outdoor area. Even then, several cloudy days can cause a significant shortfall, so extra battery capacity or another charging option is valuable.

4. Don't forget these essentials

Two 20,000 mAh USB-C power banks for phones.

Rechargeable LED lanterns and headlamps.

Battery-powered emergency radio.

Heavy-duty extension cords and a refrigerator thermometer.

Seven days of drinking water and shelf-stable food.

Battery-backup carbon monoxide detectors.

The CDC and California emergency officials recommend planning for these supplies and warn that combustion generators must only operate outdoors, at least 20 feet from openings. 
CDC
+2

Also, solar panels are not a guarantee after an earthquake: you may have debris, damaged equipment, unsafe outdoor conditions, or poor weather. Never connect a portable power station to a household wall outlet to backfeed the house.

Townhouse
What do you need to power?
Refrigerator / freezer
Internet / Wi-Fi
Phones / laptops
Lighting

Medical devices / CPAP
Heating / air conditioning
What's your budget?
$500–$1,000
$1,000–$2,000
$2,000–$4,000
$4,000+ (prioritize reliability)
Build my 7-day backup power setup

These details will help determine whether a modest battery and solar kit is enough, or whether you need a larger system to reliably get through the full week.

## 4. Don't forget these essentials

- Two 20,000 mAh USB-C power banks for phones.
- Rechargeable LED lanterns and headlamps.
- Battery-powered emergency radio.
- Heavy-duty extension cords and a refrigerator thermometer.
- Seven days of drinking water and shelf-stable food.
- Battery-backup carbon monoxide detectors.

## 5. Three questions to narrow down the purchase

{@body const [home,setHome] = DIL.useState("house")}
{@body const [loads,setLoads] = DIL.useState(["fridge","internet","phones","lights"])}
{@body const [budget,setBudget] = DIL.useState("2000-4000")}
<box border radius="xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <form gap={3} onSubmit={()=>GenUI.issueNewTurn("Recommend a specific 7-day earthquake backup power shopping list. Home: "+home+". Essentials: "+loads.join(", ")+". Budget: $"+budget+". Include battery and solar sizing, total costs, and expected runtime.")}>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What kind of home do you live in?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={home} onChange={setHome}>
        <radio value="house">House (with yard or outdoor space)</radio>
        <radio value="apartment">Apartment / condo</radio>
        <radio value="townhouse">Townhouse</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={2}>
      <label>What do you need to power?</label>
      {#each [{id:"fridge",name:"Refrigerator / freezer"},{id:"internet",name:"Internet / Wi-Fi"},{id:"phones",name:"Phones / laptops"},{id:"lights",name:"Lighting"},{id:"cooking",name:"Electric cooking"},{id:"medical",name:"Medical devices / CPAP"},{id:"heat",name:"Heating / air conditioning"}] as item}
        <checkbox key={item.id} checked={loads.includes(item.id)} onChange={v=>setLoads(old=>v?[...old,item.id]:old.filter(x=>x!==item.id))} lineThrough={false}>{item.name}</checkbox>
      {/each}
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>What's your budget?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={budget} onChange={setBudget}>
        <radio value="500-1000">$500–$1,000</radio>
        <radio value="1000-2000">$1,000–$2,000</radio>
        <radio value="2000-4000">$2,000–$4,000</radio>
        <radio value="4000+">$4,000+ (prioritize reliability)</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button block submit>Build my 7-day backup power setup <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

These details will help determine whether a modest battery and solar kit is enough, or whether you need a larger system to reliably get through the full week.
